evidence.observation: The row states: "Path and loaded-model growth outputs also matched on all 229 valid *.orm.yaml fixtures exercised on this checkout." The number appears only as the bare output line "Valid fixture pairs with byte-identical views: 229" in 003-phase-GC2.md's Gate output; none of the five recorded gates (pytest lane, ruff, two components_index calls, wheel build/install/example) produces it, no script or test in scripts/, tools/ or the suite performs the sweep, and the checkout holds 322 *.orm.yaml files, so the rule selecting the 229 "valid" ones is unrecoverable from the artifacts.

concerns.recommendation: Record the exact sweep command and the fixture-validity selection rule alongside the count (or promote the sweep to a gate or regression test) so the headline path-vs-loaded-model parity claim can be re-run and re-verified at close.
concerns.title: Fixture-parity compatibility claim is not reproducible from the record

evidence.observation: The plan requires: "Check reversed role bindings are ineligible for reuse." The only regression touching this is tests/test_growth_view.py:64-65, where `assert rec["decisions"][0]["bindings"] != {"work": "V-1", "version": "W-1"}` is logically implied by the preceding line's equality assertion and would pass for any recorded mapping; the README example hardcodes the directed bindings with a reason string, so ineligibility of the reversed assignment is demonstrated narratively via the captured span "W-1 has version V-1" and the view's role order, with no executable negative case that fails if a host records the reversed assignment against that occurrence.

concerns.recommendation: Add a negative-case regression that ties the recorded bindings to the source occurrence (for example, assert that the reversed assignment contradicts the captured span's subject-role order, or that a role-player search with swapped players cannot reproduce the occurrence), so the stated acceptance criterion is machine-checked rather than pinned only to the example's recorded value.
concerns.title: Reversed-binding ineligibility has no negative-case regression

summary: All three artifact digests match the checkout, and the load-bearing claims verify: the phase record's eight evidence-file digests match the working tree; the reported sizes reproduce exactly (fixture 16,927 source bytes, 8,864 growth bytes, 31,742 ordinary bytes, 497-byte seed view); both public surfaces exist (src/gnd/api.py:1022 for_growth keyword, src/gnd/commands/checking.py:1087 --for-growth) and share render_growth_view; docs/reference/cli.md:156 and docs/reference/python-api.md:15 document them; the pinned CLI grammar (tests/test_rf1_cli_pins.py:241) covers the flag; tests/test_growth_view.py and tests/test_growth_projection.py pin unresolved-include and stale-snapshot refusals, miss-then-role-player-hit and ambiguous deferral, partial flag plus full view digest per search, expected_model_sha256 bound to root bytes with pin reauthentication, and the family-coverage failure-on-growth assertion; the final independent review (phase-GC2-r4) is VERDICT: APPROVE. No contradiction between the claimed two-phase scope and the measured results or implementation was found. Two low concerns remain: one supplementary compatibility claim is not reproducible from the record, and one acceptance criterion lacks a negative-case regression.
